issues.legal_issue: An unregistered agreement to sell does not transfer ownership or another interest in immovable property so as to defeat recovery proceedings against the property.
material_facts: A bank initiated recovery proceedings against a company and its guarantors, and the property was attached in those proceedings.
The claimant relied on an alleged agreement to sell made before the attachment, but there was no registered deed of conveyance.
The claimant asserted that he had taken possession under the agreement.
issues.conclusion: The alleged agreement did not transfer any right, title or interest in the property and could not defeat the recovery proceedings. The limited protection under the doctrine of part performance was unavailable in this proceeding.
issues.legal_principle: Under Sections 54 and 55 of the Transfer of Property Act, an agreement to sell is not a conveyance and does not transfer title or create an interest in immovable property; a sale requires a registered instrument. Section 53A provides only a limited defence in proceedings brought by the transferor or a person claiming under the transferor. The Court relied on Suraj Lamp & Industries (P) Ltd. v. State of Haryana, (2012) 1 SCC 656.

predicates.property_recovery_proceeding: A creditor pursued recovery against a debtor or guarantor and sought to proceed against the disputed property.
predicates.alleged_sale_document_unregistered: The document relied on as a sale agreement was not a registered deed of conveyance.
predicates.claimant_relies_on_sale_agreement: The claimant relied on the agreement to assert an interest in the property.

issues.definition: When a claimant relies on an unregistered sale agreement in a property recovery proceeding, the agreement does not transfer property title.

issues.legal_issue: A disputed alleged sale agreement does not establish a prior transfer when the evidence undermines its authenticity and the claimed transaction was not disclosed by those said to have made it.
material_facts: Only a photocopy of the alleged agreement was produced, and the original was not produced.
A forensic examiner reported that the signature on the photocopy did not appear to be the purported seller’s signature.
The purported sellers did not disclose the alleged sale while challenging attachment proceedings or in communications with the housing society.
The claimant did not assert ownership during the purported seller’s lifetime and first claimed ownership after the seller’s death.
issues.conclusion: The Court found that the alleged agreement was fabricated and did not establish any transfer of rights in the property; the claimant’s claim was rejected.
issues.legal_principle: The Court assessed the reliability of the asserted transaction from the evidence and surrounding conduct, including the missing original, the forensic report and the failure to disclose the alleged sale. It applied the principle, also stated in Suraj Lamp & Industries (P) Ltd. v. State of Haryana, (2012) 1 SCC 656, that an agreement to sell is not itself a conveyance transferring title.

rule.if: property_attachment_objection_proceeding and only_photocopy_of_agreement_produced and signature_authenticity_questioned and alleged_sellers_did_not_disclose_sale and claimant_did_not_assert_ownership_during_seller_lifetime

predicates.property_attachment_objection_proceeding: A claimant objected to an attachment of property in recovery proceedings.
predicates.only_photocopy_of_agreement_produced: The claimant produced only a photocopy of the document said to record the sale, not its original.
predicates.signature_authenticity_questioned: Evidence called into question whether the purported seller signed the document.
predicates.alleged_sellers_did_not_disclose_sale: The persons said to have sold the property did not disclose the transaction when dealing with the creditor or the relevant society.
predicates.claimant_did_not_assert_ownership_during: The claimant did not assert ownership while the purported seller was alive.

issues.definition: Where an attachment objection relies on an alleged sale but the document and the parties’ conduct undermine its authenticity, the alleged transfer is not established.

issues.legal_issue: A person who has no established right, title or interest in a housing society’s property cannot claim membership on the basis of that property.
material_facts: The claimant applied to the housing society for membership based on his asserted ownership of the flat.
The asserted ownership rested on an alleged agreement that did not transfer title and was found not to establish a genuine transfer.
issues.conclusion: The claimant had no right, title or interest in the property and therefore could not claim membership of the society.
issues.legal_principle: The Court treated the claimed membership as dependent on the claimant’s asserted interest in the property. Once that interest was not established, the claimant could not claim membership on that basis; the judgment cites no separate statutory provision or earlier case for this membership conclusion.

predicates.housing_society_membership_claim: A person applied to a housing society to be admitted as a member.
predicates.claimant_relies_on_property_ownership: The person based the membership claim on asserted ownership of property associated with the society.
predicates.claimant_produced_no_valid_title_documen: The person produced no valid document establishing title to the property.

issues.definition: A person who seeks housing society membership on the basis of property ownership but produces no valid title document cannot obtain membership on that basis.
